To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spatially resolved NMR data can be evaluated using the theoretical model and transformed into material property images.

the spatial distribution of the crosslink density in a rubber network can be visualized by means of relaxation-weighted NMR images, that the crosslink density is reduced during the aging process and that the correlation time of the polymer chain dynamics is increased.
the aging process in natural rubber is accompanied by an increase in crosslink density and a reduction of chain dynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of material property NMR (MAP NMR) imaging to the study of aging processes in natural rubber.
the development of a new NMR method for the nondestructive characterization of the microstructure of polymer materials.
the investigation of material property images in the framework of aging processes in polymer networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aging process in rubber networks leads to a decrease of the mobility of the polymer chain segments and an increase of crosslink density, which is accompanied by an increase of the crosslinking density.
the aging of the material can be quantified in a spatially and temporally resolved way.
the aging process in rubber can be described in a spatially and time resolved way, using relaxation-weighted imaging techniques and suitable models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NMR imaging is able to provide information about material properties which are related to the aging process in rubber.
aging can be studied by material property (MAP)-NMR imaging.
the combination of NMR imaging with a theoretical description is an efficient tool for the investigation and characterization of the aging process in rubber networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NMR imaging can be used to investigate the material properties of rubber samples in a non-destructive way.
NMR relaxation data can be transformed into images that represent material properties.
the aging of natural rubber networks can be studied in a quantitative way using NMR imaging.
